assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour applied to a real problem: ionizable lipids that are cationic at low pH for encapsulation and near-neutral in circulation, assembled into nanoparticles with controlled microstructure. A clear physical-chemical principle (pKa-tuned charge, membrane fusion and non-bilayer phases for endosomal release) turned into a delivery technology of enormous consequence, including the mRNA vaccines and siRNA therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Hope and Madden at Vancouver (and the Inex/Acuitas line) made the foundational lipid-formulation and ionizable-lipid contributions; Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan contributed lipid design and siRNA delivery but the credit is spread over several groups. I judge Cullis, Hope and Madden the most coherent trio, with real risk that the committee prefers a different allocation.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is strong and independent (approved siRNA drug and billions of vaccine doses). Recognition is timely, though the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification overlaps in application and may affect how the committee frames the chemistry.
uncertainties: Allocation among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is contested and I cannot verify the detailed priority record.
Whether the 2023 Medicine prize makes a Chemistry prize on the delivery vehicle look derivative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a new concept of molecular organisation, expressed in the language of phase diagrams, valency, interfaces and thermodynamics, which is close to my own field. It changed how cell biology and disease (including protein aggregation and amyloid) are thought about.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman's P-granule work established the concept, and Rosen's multivalent-interaction work gave the physical-chemical framework. Pappu and Mittag are strong on sequence-to-phase-behaviour theory, so the trio is defensible but leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The concept is widely adopted but the field is still contested: in vivo claims of true liquid-like phase separation versus other assemblies, functional relevance and over-use of the term are debated. It may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Dispute over how much of the cellular phenomenology is genuine equilibrium phase separation.
Cell-biology versus chemistry character of the discovery, and Pappu and Mittag are left out.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks, using engineered deaminase-Cas fusions; it is a chemically conceived, mechanistically clear invention with clinical consequences already emerging (first patients treated).
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the clear central figure; Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees, while Nishida and Kondo made an independent cytidine-deaminase editor. A single-laureate configuration is cleanest, though Chemistry may prefer to pair it with CRISPR, which was already recognised in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and clinical translation. Recognition is timely, though some may regard it as a follow-on to the 2020 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and relation to the prime-editing candidate B011.
Credit to Nishida and Kondo versus Liu's group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to degrade proteins through the ubiquitin-proteasome system established a new pharmacological modality, with a mechanistic understanding of ternary complexes and the thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue mechanism. A real concept change in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies pioneered PROTACs; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target and so underpins molecular glues. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray and Ito are also important, so allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Many compounds are in clinical trials and the mechanism is well confirmed, but there is still no approved PROTAC drug of broad impact, so it may be a few years early.
uncertainties: Lack of approved PROTAC therapeutics so far.
Complex credit among PROTAC pioneers and molecular-glue researchers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape and funnel theory resolved Levinthal's paradox and framed protein folding in terms of statistical mechanics and thermodynamics, which is exactly the kind of general physical-chemical explanation I value. Experimental mapping connects theory to measurements.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes with Bryngelson and Onuchic originated the funnel concept; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model view; Fersht provided the experimental phi-value analysis. Fair attribution is hard and the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design changes the context.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are mature and long accepted. Timeliness is arguable since it is conceptual and its prize competitiveness is reduced by the 2024 protein-structure prize.
uncertainties: Credit among Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson, Dill and Fersht.
Whether theory without a single decisive experiment suffices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation methods extended solution NMR to proteins of high molecular weight and to protein dynamics, giving an atomic view of conformational exchange and disordered proteins. Methodologically deep and widely used, in the line of earlier NMR prizes.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore made central contributions to 3D/4D triple-resonance methods, TROSY-related approaches and dynamics; Wagner and Palmer also contributed, and Wuthrich was already recognised in 2002, which narrows novelty.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with long independent confirmation. Maybe late rather than premature, and the novelty relative to the 2002 prize is a concern.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as incremental after the 2002 NMR prize.
Allocation among Bax, Kay, Clore, Wagner and Palmer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami established programmable self-assembly of arbitrary nanoscale shapes from base-pairing rules, a clean example of design of molecular organisation with broad uses in nanomaterials and biophysics.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 scaffolded origami is the clear starting point; Yan and Shih extended it to 3D structures, and Seeman, as the founder of structural DNA nanotechnology, is not on the credited list. Winfree and Yin are also credited, so a trio is a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across hundreds of laboratories and mature as a method, though application impact is still developing and Seeman's absence complicates fair recognition.
uncertainties: Seeman's founding role and death mean the foundational credit may be seen as incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers of thiols on gold and soft lithography are interface and colloid chemistry concepts that gave precise control of surface composition and enabled much of nanoscience and biointerface research. This is near my own area of surface and self-assembly physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported alkanethiol monolayers on gold, Whitesides developed their systematic study and soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and widely used, but it may be seen as a late recognition and the scientific novelty may now seem less striking.
uncertainties: Priority dispute with Sagiv and others for the monolayer concept.
Whether the committee views it as a tool rather than a new concept.
